570a43f488239431.text: Three months later, on another Saturday at three in the morning, OpenAI went down again, but this time Tomasz's phone stayed dark and he slept right through it.

b66e87513fee9eb9.text: What had changed was that Larkfield's apps no longer called providers directly; they all called one door, a gateway, which checks who is asking and holds the keys for every provider, so the apps never have to.

7e83dd0a01f99caf.text: So I can't paste a key I never had. Got it.

96b98d5e09951a1e.text: Follow the support assistant's call through that night: it asks for support rather than for a model, because support is an alias, Larkfield's own name for a job, and the gateway looks it up in its table.

371588b34d43be62.text: The table lists OpenAI first and Anthropic second, so when OpenAI fails to answer, the gateway quietly sends the same call on to Anthropic, using a key only the gateway holds, and the customer still gets a reply.

5ec30d4e2fd66ffd.text: As Anthropic's answer goes back, the gateway writes one line in its log with the team, the alias and the tokens used, one thousand eight hundred and fifty of them, a token being a small piece of text that providers bill by.

943c47703c4041d7.text: At the end of the month Graham opens that log, and because every row carries a team's name, the single number on the invoice finally breaks down, team by team.

246e65d1ab819f01.text: Every line has a name. I could get used to this.

1cab4a2d55313053.text: And when the next new model comes out, the platform team changes one line in that table, so every app that asks for support moves to the new model without a single change of its own.

cd1362c82495a40d.text: So I can try the new model today? Today today?

931ddf13cdb2ab1f.text: Next come two short games about what you have just seen, and after them the first lab, where you send calls to a real gateway and watch what it does with them.
